Doctoral programmes
This page provides shared information about the doctoral programmes and third-cycle subject areas offered at the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS)
The School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) offers four doctoral programmes and encompasses six third-cycle subject areas.
KTH's general guidelines can be found on the page
Links and resources
. Programme-specific guidelines and information are available on each programme's page, linked below. The following overview of the structure is based on the most recent doctoral programme descriptions and the general syllabi for third-cycle subjects:
Doctoral Programme:
Computer Science
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Computer Science
Specialisation: Theoretical Computer Science
Specialisation: Robotics, Perception, and Learning
Specialisation: Computational Biology
Specialisation: High Performance Computing and Visualization
Specialisation: Network and Systems Engineering
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Speech and Music Communication
The subject has no specialisations
Doctoral Programme:
Electrical Engineering
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Electrical Engineering
Specialisation: Electromagnetics
Specialisation: Electric Power Systems
Specialisation: Information and Signal Processing
Specialisation: Micro Systems
Specialisation: Plasma Physics
Specialisation: Decision and Control Systems
Doctoral Programme:
Information and Communication Technology
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Information and Communication Technology
Specialisation: Electronic Systems
Specialisation: Integrated Devices and Circuits
Specialisation: Communication Systems
Specialisation: Software and Computer Systems
Doctoral Programme:
Mediated Communication
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Human-Computer Interaction
No specialisations
Third-Cycle Subject Area: Media Technology
Specialisation: Communication, Media Design and Cultural Theory
Specialisation: Sound and Music Computing
Specialisation: Visual Technology
Doctoral students are required to adhere to KTH's general guidelines for third-cycle studies, fulfill the criteria outlined in the general syllabi for their respective subject areas, and establish as well as follow up on their individual study plans (ISPs).
Expectation form
To get a good understanding of the mutual expectations between student and supervisor, concerning doctoral studies and supervision, the following form can be used as a starting point for the discussions. It is recommended to do this at an early stage, but also to revisit the document later as the studies progress. Please indicate in Section 6.1 in the ISP as a comment to the first progress meeting whether you have used the form for aligning expectations upon preparing the initial ISP.
